title: Smooth scheduler jitter and consolidate KV hot-path into unified read path
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observed periodic scheduler jitter and tail-latency amplification under moderate spike patterns. Investigation shows multiple fast-paths reading from our key-value session cache (separate hotpath for prefetch, another for in-flight reads, plus a fallback cold path) introduce duplicated synchronization, divergent metrics, and brittle prewarming semantics. The goal of this ticket is to: 1) smooth scheduler timing to reduce jitter at the batch-formation boundary, and 2) merge the KV fast-paths into a single coherent, lock-minimal read path with clear invariants and metrics.

Motivation / Impact:
- Reduce 95/99th token generation latency by eliminating oscillations in batch boundaries.
- Improve effective cache hit rate by standardizing warmup semantics, reducing redundant prefetch attempts.
- Simplify future optimizations (e.g., speculative KV warmup and unified telemetry) and lower cognitive overhead for on-call engineers.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 end-to-end generation latency decreases by >=6% on synthetic spike workload compared to baseline; P99 decrease is a secondary goal but should not regress.
- KV cache hit-rate for medium-length sessions (avg seq len 512) increases or stays flat; no >1% drop in hit rate.
- No increase in CPU utilization >8% at steady state on canary nodes.
- All new code covered by unit tests and integration tests; documented in design doc and linked PR.
- Canary rollout plan executed with automatic rollback if error rate or p95 regresses beyond thresholds.

Design notes / approach:
1) Scheduler jitter smoothing:
   - Replace current fixed-timer boundary used by the ingress coalescer with a watermark-driven soft-delay. New approach computes a dynamic micro-delay based on inflight queue variance and historical inter-arrival times. This reduces bursty boundary effects while preserving low-latency for single-request cases.
   - Introduce a bounded credit mechanism so a sudden flood doesn't stall existing lanes; credits are replenished at token emission events.

2) KV hot-path consolidation:
   - Build a single ReadPath component that handles prefetch, in-flight lookup, and fallback to async refill. The component exposes a tiny, lock-free fast path for hits (atomic read of pointer + version check) and a guarded slow-path that takes a lightweight mutex only when necessary.
   - Remove duplicated prefetch callers; move prefetch initiation responsibility to the ReadPath with explicit idempotency guards.
   - Introduce a concise contract: callers get either (hit, revision) or (miss, request_handle). Revision numbers are monotonic per session to enable safe racing with background compaction.

Trade-offs considered:
- Replacing multiple optimized but divergent fast-paths with a unified read path risks a small regression in the absolute fastest micro-path. We mitigate this by benchmarking the new atomic fast path heavily and keeping the old path behind a feature flag for quick rollback.
- Watermark smoothing introduces a tiny micro-delay on some edge single-request flows; we tune the soft-delay upper bound to keep P50 impact <1ms.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: Prototype ReadPath in isolation with unit tests and microbench harness. (ENG-877778)
- Week 2: Integrate ReadPath into batcher read adapters; implement watermark-driven scheduling logic (ENG-877779).
- Week 3: End-to-end integration tests + perf runs on CI; iterate on parameters.
- Week 4: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in dedicated pool, monitor dashboards and automatic rollback checks.

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Microbench: atomic fast-path latency, slow-path cold misses, mutex contention under synthetic hotkey patterns.
- End-to-end: token-per-second and latency p50/p95/p99 under steady and spike workloads. Use the existing perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-perf/tree/main/benchmarks (PR will reference actual commit).

Rollout & Monitoring:
- Canary target: dedicated pool 'dedicated-canary-small' for 5% of traffic.
- Key dashboards: generation-latency (p50/p95/p99), kv-hitrate-by-session-length, batch-sizes histogram, cpu-util, request-errors. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/cluster-latency-2026 (placeholder).
- Rollback criteria: p95 latency increase >5% for 10m or error rate >0.1% sustained for 5m.

Risks & mitigations:
- Regressed hot-path latency: keep old implementation toggled via runtime flag for fast rollback.
- Increased memory pressure from new ReadPath metadata: pre-calc memory budget and run long-lived soak tests.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ReadPath+Consolidation+&+Scheduler+Smoothing (internal).
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6184 (WIP).
- Perf runs: results attached to the PR and pushed to the perf bucket.

Next steps / open questions:
- Decide final versioning semantics for per-session revision numbers (atomic counter vs epoch stamping). Proposal leaning toward monotonic epoch to simplify compaction racing.
- Validate credit refill policy under mixed long/short session mixes.

Owner notes:
- This ticket intentionally groups scheduler smoothing and KV fast-path consolidation because they interact at the batch formation boundary; separating them increased churn in prior attempts. If scope grows, split into two follow-ups (see sub_issues).
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after correlating spike runs with profiler traces. Attached initial flamegraphs and sample traces in design doc.

2026-02-23 - Liam O'Connor: POC for ReadPath atomic fast-path implemented. Microbench shows 0.6us median for fast-path vs 0.5us prior — within acceptable range. Pushed WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6184.
2026-02-26 - Chen Wei (review): Suggested removing a double-check pattern that caused ABA risk; recommended using 64-bit revision stamping. Left inline review comments on PR.
2026-03-01 - Liam O'Connor: Addressed Chen's feedback; switched to 64-bit monotonic epoch, added unit tests for contention window. Added feature flag 'readpath_unified' to runtime flags.

2026-03-05 - QA (Maya Singh): Ran synthetic spike harness; observed p95 drop of 7.2% and p99 flat. Noted small increase in CPU (4%) during cold starts. Added integration test for prefetch idempotency.
2026-03-10 - SRE (Jordan Blake): Reviewed canary plan, added alert thresholds and circuit breaker hooks. Approved canary for 5% rollout starting 2026-03-15.
2026-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Finalized PR with docs and perf artifacts. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-15. Remaining tasks: tighten soft-delay tunables and add more soak runs (see sub_issues).
